title: The $230-a-Week Rule That Fixed Theo's Budget

scenes.say: Theo takes home $4,000 a month, and runs out by day 20.
Bills, savings and spending all come out of one account. So he never knows what's safe to spend.
So he splits it. Fixed bills first: about $2,400 on autopay.
Then $600 to savings, the day he gets paid.
What's left is $1,000 a month, about $230 a week.
Groceries, gas, fun, all from that $230. When it's gone, the week is done.
Same paycheck. Now about $7,200 saved in a year.
What would your weekly number be? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because $4,000 shouldn't mean broke by day 20.

question: Take your everyday money and divide it by weeks: what's your weekly number?
description: Theo takes home about $4,000 a month and used to run out by day 20. He put about $2,400 of fixed bills on autopay, moved $600 to savings on payday and spends from a weekly number of about $230. That's roughly $7,200 saved in a year on the same pay. Numbers are rounded US estimates.
